title: Global dimension bound for localized fibres
statement: Let R → S be a finite type map of commutative rings and g ∈ S. If every prime q in D(g) has local fibre dimension at most d, then every nonempty fibre of S_g has Krull dimension at most d.

source.place: Tags 00DK, 00DL and 00E4, used in Tag 00ST proof (3)

proof.text: For each base prime p set k = κ(p), F = k tensor_R S and a = 1 tensor g. Apply IsLocalization.Away.tensorProductEquivTMulRight to identify the localized fibre k tensor_R S_g with F_a, and take the homeomorphism of prime spectra induced by this ring equivalence.

The contraction f : Spec F_a → Spec F is an open embedding with range D(a). For a point Qg let Q = f(Qg); then a is not in Q. Use the inverse of PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber to obtain its corresponding prime q of S over p. The inverse contracts along includeRight, so g is not in q. Surjectivity of the fibre equivalence and substitution of q ∩ R = p allow hV to give local dimension at Q at most d. This reindexing is the proved private helper fibre_bound_at_fixed_base.

For any inducing map f, pull back an open neighbourhood U of f(x). The restricted map from its inverse image into U is inducing, so Topology.IsInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le bounds its global dimension by that of U. Taking infima gives the local-dimension inequality, proved in the private helper dimAt_inducing_le. This applies even to noninjective, nonsurjective inducing maps. Apply it to the fibre homeomorphism and the homeomorphism onto the localization embedding range. The open-subspace local-dimension equality identifies the dimension in that range with that at Q in Spec F. Combine with step 2 to bound each point of the localized fibre by d.

Rewrite the dimension of the localized fibre as the supremum of its pointwise local dimensions and apply iSup_le to the bounds in step 3. An empty spectrum gives an empty supremum, so the supplied nontriviality hypothesis is not needed by the proof; its statement is retained unchanged.
